info.title: KineticCT API
info.summary: Programmatic access to a self-hosted KineticCT installation.
info.description:
Versioned REST API for KineticCT. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`; session cookies are not accepted here.

**Authorization** combines the API key's scopes with the role of the account that issued it: an administrator-issued key still needs the matching scope for every call, and scopes alone never grant administrator rights.

**Responses** are `{ data, meta }` on success and `{ error: { code, message, request_id } }` on failure. Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header.

**Capabilities** are reported honestly: `/api/v1/capabilities` states what this installation supports, and unsupported operations fail with explicit codes instead of pretending to succeed.

bearerAuth.description: A KineticCT API key (`kct_live_…`). Create one in the panel under Administration → API Keys.

Meta.description: Response metadata. Every `/api/v1` JSON response carries the id that produced it.

ErrorObject.description: Machine-readable code, human message, and the request id. `details` is present on validation and scope errors.

code.description: Stable error code (see docs/API.md for the full list).

message.example: This API key does not have permission to perform this operation.

Capabilities.description: What this installation can actually do. Limitations are stated explicitly instead of failing later.

User.description: Public user fields. Password hashes and session tokens are never returned.

LiveState.description: Reconciled host state. `exists: null` means the host could not be checked — never guessed.

EffectiveConfig.description: Limits as the host actually applies them, plus storage and lxcfs facts.

Network.description: Live network facts read from the host (interfaces, addresses, gateway).

Node.description: Node record. `api_token` is stored server-side and never returned.

managed.description: False for host containers KineticCT does not track.

ApiKey.description: API key metadata. The plaintext secret exists only in the create/rotate response and is never stored or returned again.

created_by_key.description: Parent key id when created through the API.

secret.description: The full plaintext key. Shown once — copy it now; it cannot be retrieved later.

Operation.description: A recorded infrastructure operation with honest state transitions.

type.description: instance.create | instance.delete | instance.action | instance.repair | instance.resources_update | node.create | node.delete

detail.description: Redacted: credential-like keys are replaced with [redacted].

api_key.description: Present for Bearer-authenticated calls: the calling key's own identity and scopes.

ScopeCatalogue.description: The authoritative scope list used by enforcement, the admin UI, and this document.
